questions.question: When exiting your vehicle, you must maintain ____ with the vehicle at all times.

options.text: One point of contact
Four points of contact
Three points of contact
Two points of contact

questions.explanation: During the basic vehicle control skills test, face the vehicle and keep three points of contact at all times. For a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly will result in automatic failure.

questions.question: How many hazardous materials classes are there?

options.text: Four
Six
Nine
Two

questions.explanation: There are nine classes of hazardous materials. Each class shows the type of danger the material poses.

questions.question: When asked to make a lane change during the skills test, you should:

options.text: Make the necessary traffic checks first.
Not use your mirrors.
Cut off other vehicles if needed to follow the instructions.
Not make the lane change if you don't want to.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make the necessary traffic checks first.
questions.explanation: You will make multiple lane changes during the driving skills test. Check traffic and signal before changing lanes. Change lanes smoothly when it is safe.

questions.question: Shippers must label hazardous materials. If an item is smaller than its label, how should the item be labeled?

options.text: The item may be tied together with other hazardous materials and labeled with a sheet of paper on the outside of the bundle.
The label may be attached to a tag that is securely attached to the package.
The item may be marked with a large orange dot.
The item may be placed in a box displaying a warning label.

questions.correctAnswerText: The label may be attached to a tag that is securely attached to the package.
questions.explanation: Shippers must place diamond-shaped hazard warning labels on hazardous materials packages. If the label doesn't fit on the package, attach it to a securely fastened tag.

questions.question: Load hazardous materials:

options.text: Near heat sources.
Away from heat sources.
In direct sunlight.
In the rain.

questions.explanation: Always load hazardous materials away from heat sources. Heat can make many materials more dangerous.

questions.question: When driving a vehicle with empty cargo tanks that are used to carry hazardous materials, the driver:

options.text: Can cross railroad tracks without slowing or stopping.
Needs to slow when approaching railroad tracks, but is not required to stop.
Must stop at railroad crossings before proceeding.
Should never drive over railroad tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop at railroad crossings before proceeding.
questions.explanation: A vehicle with tanks used to transport hazardous materials must always stop at railroad crossings before crossing, even if the tanks are empty.

questions.question: If your vehicle is equipped with a cargo lift, you should ensure that:

options.text: The lift is loosely attached.
The lift is not leaking.
The lift is fully extended.
The lift is the proper color.

questions.explanation: During your vehicle inspection test, check the cargo lift for leaks, damage, or missing parts. The lift must be fully retracted and locked securely.

questions.question: If a product requires a "Poison Inhalation Hazard" placard, the placard must be used when transporting:

options.text: More than 50 pounds of the product.
More than 10 pounds of the product.
Any amount of the product.
The product in a non-sealed container.

questions.explanation: For materials requiring a "Poison Inhalation Hazard" placard, you must display the placard and the appropriate hazard class placard at all times, even for small amounts.

questions.question: When driving through a curve during the skills test, you should:

options.text: Veer from your lane if needed to complete the curve.
Reduce your speed after entering the curve.
Refrain from looking for other vehicles while turning.
Reduce your speed before entering the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed before entering the curve.
questions.explanation: Before entering a curve during the on-road driving skills test, slow down enough so you don't need to brake or shift while turning. Stay in your lane and check for traffic in all directions.

questions.question: When taking the basic vehicle control skills test:

options.text: Points are deducted for each pull-up.
A driver is allowed three pull-ups per maneuver.
A pull-up will earn points only if the driver gets out of the vehicle before pulling up.
Only an excessive number of pull-ups will be counted as errors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only an excessive number of pull-ups will be counted as errors.
questions.explanation: During the basic vehicle control skills test, one pull-up has no penalty. However, too many pull-ups will count as errors.

questions.question: If corrosive materials leak in the trailer, how should it be cleaned?

options.text: Clean with acid.
Clean with water.
Leave it to air-dry without washing.
Clean with bleach.

questions.explanation: Any vehicle part that touches corrosive material must be washed thoroughly with water.

questions.question: The person loading a tank with hazardous materials must have all of these qualities except:

options.text: Be alert.
Stay within 10 feet of the tank.
Understand the hazards of the materials.
Be authorized to move the tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay within 10 feet of the tank.
questions.explanation: The supervisor of loading or unloading a hazardous materials tank must be alert, have a clear view of the tank, stay within 25 feet of the tank, know the hazards, know emergency procedures, and be authorized and able to move the tank.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, what must you NOT do regarding oil?

options.text: Show where the dipstick is located.
Show that oil level is within a safe range.
Show that oil level is above the refill mark.
Show that oil level is below the refill mark.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show that oil level is below the refill mark.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must show where the dipstick is, prove the oil is in a safe range, and show the oil is above the refill mark.

questions.question: How should hazardous materials placards be used on a vehicle?

options.text: Only for explosives.
On all four sides of the vehicle.
Only by Class A licensed drivers.
To reduce insurance rates.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all four sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials warning placards must be placed on all four sides of any vehicle carrying hazardous materials.

questions.question: How should identification numbers, shipping names, and hazard classes appear on shipping papers?

options.text: They can be abbreviated if space is limited.
They can be abbreviated to make them easier to read.
They should never be abbreviated.
They can be abbreviated if the abbreviations are easy to understand.

questions.explanation: Identification numbers, shipping names, and hazard classes must never be abbreviated on shipping papers. The only exception is if the abbreviation is specifically authorized in hazardous materials regulations.

questions.question: Where must hazardous materials placards be placed on a truck?

options.text: On the rear only.
On the left and right sides only.
On the front only.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Hazardous materials placards must be placed on all four sides of the vehicle.

questions.question: During the steering box inspection, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Check that the steering box is securely mounted.
Check that the steering box has no leaks.
Look for missing bolts in the steering box.
Assume all cotter keys are present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume all cotter keys are present.
questions.explanation: Check that the steering box is securely mounted, look for missing nuts, bolts, and cotter keys, and check for power steering fluid leaks and damaged hoses.

questions.question: Which statement about a person supervising tank loading is true?

options.text: They do not need to be able to move the vehicle.
They must be a licensed firefighter.
They do not need to know about the materials being loaded.
They must stay within 25 feet of the tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: They must stay within 25 feet of the tank.
questions.explanation: A tank loading supervisor must be alert, have a clear view of the tank, stay within 25 feet of the tank, know the hazards of the materials, know emergency procedures, and be authorized and able to move the tank.

questions.question: After stopping during the stop/start maneuver, what should you do?

options.text: Use the four-way flashers.
Do not use four-way flashers because it is a test, not an emergency.
Leave the vehicle in first gear.
Park in front of a fire hydrant.

questions.explanation: After stopping during the stop/start maneuver, activate your four-way flashers and shift into neutral or park. Do not block driveways, intersections, fire hydrants, or signs.

questions.question: What does a material's hazard class tell you?

options.text: The risks of the material.
How quickly the material must reach its destination.
How much the material weighs.
The country where the material came from.

questions.explanation: Hazardous materials fall into nine different hazard classes. Each class reflects the specific risks of that material.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, the landing gear should be:

options.text: Retracted.
Fully raised.
More worn on the passenger's side than on the driver's side.
Well lit.

questions.explanation: During a trailer inspection, check that the landing gear is fully raised with no missing parts. The crank handle must be secure and the support frame must not be damaged.

questions.question: To choose the right placards, you need to know:

options.text: The hazard classes of the materials.
The types of containers holding the materials.
The destination.
The shipper.

questions.correctAnswerText: The hazard classes of the materials.
questions.explanation: To choose the correct hazardous materials placards, you must know the hazard class of the materials, the amount being shipped, and the total weight of all hazardous materials in the vehicle.

questions.question: When entering traffic on an expressway during the skills test, you should:

options.text: Check for traffic.
Not use signals.
Abruptly enter a lane of traffic.
Cut off other drivers if needed.

questions.explanation: During the driving skills test on an expressway, check traffic, use proper signals, and merge smoothly into the correct lane.

questions.question: What symbol shows a marine pollutant?

options.text: Waves in a yellow triangle with an X through the waves.
A fish in a white triangle with an X through the fish.
A light blue square with a dark blue X through it.
A bird in a red octagon.

questions.correctAnswerText: A fish in a white triangle with an X through the fish.
questions.explanation: The marine pollutant symbol is a fish in a white triangle with an X through the fish.

questions.question: During the basic vehicle control skills test:

options.text: A pull-up always counts against the applicant.
A pull-up should be completed at least once.
Stopping without changing direction is not a pull-up.
Excessive pull-ups are acceptable in some test administrators' opinions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping without changing direction is not a pull-up.
questions.explanation: A pull-up occurs when you stop and pull forward to get a better position. Simply stopping without changing direction is not a pull-up. Too many pull-ups will count as errors.

questions.question: What is used to warn people about hazardous materials?

options.text: Placards.
Flashing lights.
Color-coded tape.
License plate stickers.

questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped warning signs called placards are placed on the outside of vehicles carrying hazardous materials to warn people.

questions.question: A driver must take the HazMat knowledge test:

options.text: Once every year.
Before every CDL renewal.
Once every 10 years.
Only once.

questions.explanation: You must pass the HazMat knowledge test and pass a federal background check before every CDL renewal.

questions.question: What does a hazardous materials shipping paper describe?

options.text: The materials being transported.
How the materials will be transported.
Who should accept the materials.
The cost of the materials.

questions.explanation: A shipping paper describes the hazardous materials being transported. Examples include shipping orders, bills of lading, and manifests.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, lug nuts should be all of the following, except:

options.text: Free of cracks.
Free of distortions.
Loose.
Free of rust.

questions.explanation: All lug nuts must be present and free of cracks, distortions, and rust. Check for signs of looseness like rust trails or shiny threads. All bolt holes must be free of cracks and distortions.

questions.question: When alley docking, your vehicle should be parked:

options.text: With the front bumper on the front boundary line.
With the rear wheels over the rear boundary line.
Straight within the boundaries of the parking space.
At an angle within the boundaries of the parking space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straight within the boundaries of the parking space.
questions.explanation: To alley dock, pull past the alley and stop parallel to the outer boundary. Back your vehicle straight into the parking area. Your vehicle must be parked straight within the boundaries of the space.
